transform_notes: SAP's own key is a Plant/Location combination (T499S-WERKS + STORT).
Needs a real Plant determination from the target org structure, not just a Company Code -- same recurring gap as Sales Orders>Company_ID and Inventory Items>Company_ID.
No standard 'old code' field on T499S the way MARA has BISMT. Kept only as the Location_ID staging key's companion -- not loaded separately.
Investigated before mapping: Location_Name's embedded place name agrees with the City column on all 10 rows, which is why City (not the Address field) is used for geography below.

This determines WHICH SAP object the location even becomes -- a value of 'Plant' plausibly means an actual SAP Plant (T001W) rather than just a T499S location entry, 'Warehouse' could mean a Storage Location (T001L) or WM Warehouse Number (T300). Not a value to look up, a genuine object-routing decision that needs to be made per distinct Location_Type before any of these rows can be loaded correctly.

Checked before mapping: the trailing city token in this free-text field disagrees with the declared City column on 9/10 rows -- but the STREET portion itself isn't part of what was shown unreliable, only the embedded city. Use split_delimiter part_index 0 for STREET; do NOT use part_index 1 for city (see City below).

Opposite resolution from Customers>Country: here the standalone City column is the one corroborated by an independent field (Location_Name) and the free-text address is the unreliable one. Use City directly for CITY1, and derive COUNTRY from City via the same value_map reference table as Customers (Amman/Aqaba/Irbid/etc. -> JO, Dubai -> AE, ...).

Checked: agrees with City on 10/10 rows (unlike Customers>Country), so it's reliable here -- but COUNTRY is already derived from City via value_map above, making this column redundant rather than a second source of truth. Could be used directly instead of the City-derivation as an equally valid alternative; not mapped twice.

Same block/deletion-flag ambiguity as Customers>Is_Active and Inventory Items>Is_Active -- SAP has no single active flag, and all 10 rows are True here, giving no evidence of which indicator 'inactive' would need to mean.
